stories.summary: A design-only Crèche manifest now defines 30 proposed visual states, including 22 required and eight optional, for a realistic PBR-rendered 2D scene. Existing gameplay and art registration remain unchanged; visual approvals and production are still ahead.
stories.body: Commit 0d41ea40 publishes a Crèche layered PBR design manifest with depth bands from exterior and floor through fixtures, local effects and foreground occlusion. It preserves Godot's existing 2D gameplay and collision ownership while specifying orthographic 3D-rendered art, source registration and animation states. The 30 states are design inventory, not completed assets. The commit explicitly says no Asset V2 registry change, human visual approval or runtime cutover occurred. Commit message reports GitHub Validate Repository PASS, but the combined status endpoint returned no checks; independent validation was not verified. Operational dispatcher totals remain unavailable.
bullets: 30 proposed Crèche visual states: 22 required and eight optional.
Orthographic 3D/PBR rendering targets existing Godot 2D layers.
Existing runtime art and gameplay remain unchanged.
Human visual approval and Asset V2 registration are still pending.

article.lead: The Crèche of Answerless Names has a more precise visual production blueprint. A new manifest describes how to build realistic, depth-separated scenery and animation without replacing CUSTODIAN's existing 2D gameplay. It is a design milestone, not an art delivery.

sections.heading: Real depth without a gameplay-engine migration
sections.text: The proposal uses orthographic renders of modeled stone, metal and machinery, split into floor, structural, fixture, effect and foreground layers. Godot keeps ownership of movement, collision and interactions.

sections.heading: A roadmap, not a runtime cutover
sections.text: The manifest specifies 30 proposed visual states, 22 required and eight optional. Existing asset families and gameplay are untouched; the new design has not been registered as production art or visually approved.

insights.title: Layer separation makes animation practical
insights.explanation: Keeping machines, floor and foreground occlusion independent allows localized effects and character overlap without repainting the entire room for every animation frame.

insights.title: The next bottleneck is approval and registration
insights.explanation: The plan is now detailed enough to guide production, but none of its new visual states should be counted as delivered or active in-game.

article.takeaway: The Crèche's proposed art architecture is documented; asset creation, visual approval, registration and runtime validation remain distinct future gates.
article.next_watch: Watch for approved first source plates, registered Asset V2 states and an in-game validation showing correct alpha, depth and interaction alignment.

stories.headline: Browser reply reader lands with unfinished return paths
stories.summary: A new read-only ChatGPT browser adapter landed on main to help CUSTODIAN orchestration collect completed replies. Code inspection finds debugging return paths that break its stated output contract; validation and live operation are not established.
stories.body: Commit f42cc51 adds get_chatgpt_response.py v1.1.0, attaching through an existing local Chrome debugging endpoint and reading visible conversation DOM. The implementation documents a strict completed-text / RESPONSE IN PROGRESS / error contract, but read_once currently returns 'FIRST DOT GET BUSY' when generation is active, returns a page object when reply text is empty, and emits a debugging placeholder on an unexpected probe result. These paths contradict the documented interface and may confuse orchestration consumers. This is a verified source-level defect, not proof of an observed runtime failure. No tests, independent acceptance, running process, or teardown were verified. The private pilot observation pointer was last modified earlier than this commit and is not fresh evidence of this state.
bullets: Read-only browser reply adapter added to main.
Three return paths conflict with its documented stdout contract.
No runtime failure or CI success inferred from source alone.
Correct contract branches and validate before wiring into orchestration.

article.lead: CUSTODIAN now has a browser-side reader intended to collect completed ChatGPT responses for its orchestration loop. The new script is on main, but its current source contains unfinished return paths that could mislead the next automation step.

sections.heading: A bridge from browser conversations to orchestration
sections.text: The adapter attaches to an existing Chrome debugging session, identifies a conversation and reads visible assistant text. It is designed to avoid private application APIs and report whether a reply has finished.

sections.heading: The contract and the code diverge
sections.text: The script promises either completed text, a standard in-progress marker, or a nonzero error. Instead, an active reply can return a debugging phrase; an empty reply can return a browser page object; and an unexpected probe state returns a placeholder. These are source-confirmed inconsistencies, not observed production failures.

insights.title: A small protocol mismatch can stall a large art pipeline
insights.explanation: An orchestrator needs reliable completion signals before fetching and installing generated assets. Ambiguous output can turn a finished response into a false success or a stuck handoff.

insights.title: Landing is not validation
insights.explanation: The commit proves the adapter exists on main. It does not establish tests, independent acceptance, or a running browser connection.

article.takeaway: The new bridge is a useful integration point, but its response contract needs correction and tests before consumers rely on it.
article.next_watch: Watch for a follow-up patch restoring the documented return values and a bounded test of completed, streaming, empty, and ambiguous replies.

stories.headline: A reviewer PASS is preserved, but missing session metadata blocks acceptance
stories.summary: A source-mode correction review has a preserved reviewer PASS message and successful host-validation recovery, but its continuation metadata lacks a required ordinal. CUSTODIAN has admitted a narrowly scoped repair and independent-review pair to the ready queue. No acceptance or recovery apply has occurred.
stories.body: The new continuation-ordinal recovery packet documents a reviewer session that exited successfully after host-validation attempt two, yet strict outcome verification rejects its missing continuation_number. The repair is designed to correct future metadata writing and authenticate the one historical run without editing original evidence or relaunching a reviewer. Commit 55fbb7ff marks the implementation and dependent independent review ready/auto. These are queue states, not proof of host execution. Independent acceptance of the earlier source-mode review remains unverified. The private observation pointer is dated earlier than the current main changes, so no fresh operational counts are admitted.
bullets: New recovery implementation and dependent review are ready/auto.

Recovery apply is explicitly deferred until independent review is archived complete.
Host process, teardown and full dispatcher counts remain unknown.

article.lead: CUSTODIAN has uncovered a subtle reason a successful reviewer session still cannot count as an accepted review: its continuation record lacks a required sequence number. A narrowly bounded repair and a separate independent review have now entered the dispatch queue.

sections.heading: The verdict exists, but the proof chain is incomplete
sections.text: The recovery packet describes a reviewer process that exited successfully with a saved PASS message after host validation recovered. The strict verifier refuses to authenticate that result because continuation metadata omits the required ordinal. A PASS message alone cannot substitute for verified session provenance.

sections.heading: A repair with a deliberately narrow scope
sections.text: The new implementation is intended to fix future metadata and reconstruct only the named historical session using authenticated evidence. Its paired reviewer must test tampering, replay and mismatched-session rejection before any protected recovery is authorized.

insights.title: Review completion and review acceptance are different events
insights.explanation: A reviewer may finish and write a verdict while the coordinator still cannot safely establish which authenticated session produced it. The new packet addresses that evidence boundary, not the review's technical judgment.

insights.title: Ready is not running
insights.explanation: The latest commit changes packet dispatch eligibility. It does not establish a worker claim, live execution, accepted PASS or clean teardown.

article.takeaway: A bounded provenance repair is queued; the preserved review remains unaccepted until independently validated recovery proves the exact session.
article.next_watch: Watch for the implementation landing, its independent acceptance, and only then a separately authorized exact-run recovery.

stories.headline: Executable-source archive correction lands; independent review is next
stories.summary: CUSTODIAN has landed and archived a targeted correction for validating already-executable Python sources in paired-review archives. The implementation reports 294 passing tests, but independent acceptance and host cleanup remain unverified.
stories.body: The source-bearing archive validator now permits a Python source file to retain executable mode only when explicitly authorized and executable throughout its authenticated history. Commit cd1cff49 carries the implementation and reported validation; commits 814e6779 and a5275416 mark and archive the implementation packet complete. The separate review packet remains ready, not accepted. No full dispatcher audit, host teardown receipt, or CI conclusion was established. The private pilot pointer is older than the current main changes and exact-byte validation is unavailable, so no operational counts were admitted.

article.lead: A narrow repair to CUSTODIAN’s paired-review archive validator has reached main. It allows a legitimate Python source file to remain executable across an authenticated archive history without allowing new or unauthorized executable files through.

sections.heading: The repair is now part of main
sections.text: The implementation was committed and its task packet marked complete and archived. Its accompanying summary reports 294 passing tests and complete changed-file validation, including adversarial file-mode cases.

sections.heading: Independent scrutiny still matters
sections.text: A separate review packet is ready with a source-specific checkout profile. That reviewer must independently reconstruct the historical WIRE archive case and test that unsafe mode changes remain rejected. Ready is not accepted, and neither proves a live worker or clean teardown.

insights.title: A file permission was blocking a larger recovery chain
insights.explanation: The validator previously treated an already-executable source file as disallowed archive content. This targeted exception may unblock review of the WIRE exporter without weakening restrictions on metadata and newly executable files, provided independent review confirms the implementation.

article.takeaway: The correction is landed and its implementation packet is archived; independent review acceptance remains the decisive next gate.
article.next_watch: Watch for an independently accepted review receipt, then an explicitly authorized recovery of the protected WIRE review.
